# v0.3.2 — Scan memory safety, review blockers and a restore point you can see

## Browser/messenger scans no longer materialize file lists

Sizing a cache directory collected every file path into a vector before
summing — 6 GB of cache meant hundreds of thousands of `PathBuf`s on the
heap, so the **scan** could still exhaust memory even though the clean was
fixed in 0.2.1. Sizes now stream through a dedicated `dir_size` walker
(u64 accumulator, no vectors), and the deep-cache size walk goes 14 levels
down instead of 10, so deep `CacheStorage` trees stop being underreported.

## Restore point: a conscious step, not a ghost-window cascade

Creating the restore point silently chained an elevated PowerShell, a UAC
prompt and `Checkpoint-Computer`'s own dialogs — three Windows surfaces
mid-click that looked like malware and permanently zeroed a
system-wide policy. Now:

- The mandatory **.reg backup** stays (silent, reversible with
  `reg import`).
- The fix dialog offers **"Open System Protection"**, launching the native
  Windows *Create a restore point* applet.
- The **Fix button stays disabled** until you confirm the restore point
  was created — an informed decision instead of a hidden side effect.
- No hidden elevation, no PowerShell cascade, no system policy writes.

## Closing browsers is honest about force

Closing browsers force-quits whatever outlives the graceful close
(extension and background processes keep cache files locked — that was
killing the clean). The dialog now says so explicitly, and the grace
period doubled to 4 seconds before force-termination.

## WSL scans only your Windows profile

The Linux build under WSL used to scan **every** profile under
`/mnt/c/Users` — including other people's accounts. It now resolves the
current user through the Windows interop and scans that profile alone;
with interop unavailable, no Windows data is scanned at all.

## Other fixes from the review

- Registry fix progress is real now: one key at a time, after the backup —
  no more bar at 100% while the slow part runs
- Disk metrics prefer the `SystemDrive` volume on Windows instead of the
  first disk in the list (which could be a recovery partition)
- Uninstall toasts say the **wizard started** instead of claiming the app
  was already uninstalled
- Backend error messages no longer mix Portuguese and English
